description:
Measure before building anything. Output: docs/research/simd.md.

- For every kernel in examples/ (and bench/), record clang's vectorisation verdict (use Defk, report: :full) and time, on arm64 (baseline, then armv8.2-a / -mcpu=native) and on real x86-64 hardware (baseline SSE2, x86-64-v2, x86-64-v3, -march=native). No emulated timings (qemu/Rosetta numbers don't count).
- Classify what blocks vectorisation where it doesn't happen: remaining per-operation checks (e.g. defk-agp), in-order float reductions (bit-exactness, by design), early exits, gathers, index arithmetic, safepoints.
- Check that each -march level keeps float results bit-exact with Elixir mode (FMA stays off under -ffp-contract=off? denormals? libm differences?) by running the agreement suite built at each level.
- List the measured gaps to BIFs/NIFs (CRC, UTF-8 validation, substring search, hashes, base64) and say for each whether target flags, a hardware builtin or vector types would close it.
- Survey prior art: Zig @Vector, Wasm SIMD128, Rust std::simd/portable_simd, Go's lack of SIMD, Julia, ISPC; Erlang/OTP's own CPU-feature handling (JIT, crypto); how Rustler/precompiled NIFs ship per-target artifacts (rustler_precompiled targets, NIF version matrix).

Done when the doc has the tables and a recommendation for which of the prototype tickets are worth doing.

comments.text:
Research landed on branch defk-ulk.1/simd-research (0592fd9): docs/research/simd.md, tools in bench/simd/ (CC wrapper per level; no lib/ change), performance.md 6.14, 6.15 and a 7.1 note.

Findings (M4 Pro, Apple clang 21, loaded machine, provisional):
- Vectorisation: 24 of 200 catalogue loops vectorise, identical loop by loop and width at default (apple-m1), generic, armv8.2-a and -mcpu=native. Blockers: loop-carried recurrences (hashes, CRC, DFA, Myers) are most; then early exits from remaining checks, gathers (codecs), early-exit-by-design loops, branchy bodies.
- arm64 timing, 42 kernels, interleaved, 3 runs: native and armv8.2-a within about ±3% of default everywhere. -mcpu=generic: sort_i64 0.78x, cosine/keccak 0.93x, SHA-256 1.18x faster. -mtune=generic alone reproduces it and -march=armv8-a alone does not, so it is tuning, not features.
- x86-64 (remarks only): SSE2 14 loops vectorised, v2 16, v3/v4 20 at double width; ws_mask's main loop vectorises only at v3+; sum, dot and cosine never vectorise on x86 (no ordered reductions).
- Bit-exactness: 331 agreement/float tests pass with kernels built at generic, armv8.2-a and native. The 42 kernels agree with Elixir mode and with the default build at every level. No FMA at any level, including x86-64-v3/v4, under -ffp-contract=off; the contract=on control shows FMAs. No FPCR/MXCSR use.
- Gaps: no flag emits CRC32/SHA/SHA3 instructions. CRC32C needs a builtin (14x gap). UTF-8, base64/hex and substring search need vector values.
- Recommendation, in order: ulk.4 (crc32c) first; then ulk.5 (ceiling study); then the x86 timing run; ulk.2 only if x86 v3 gains are real (arm64 says no; consider -mtune separately); ulk.3 last.

NOT DONE (why the ticket stays open): x86-64 timings, which need real hardware. On an x86-64 Linux box with clang:
  mix deps.get; uptime; SIMD_CC=clang mix run bench/simd/time.exs 9 /tmp/simd-x86.etf
  SIMD_CC=clang bench/simd/agree_levels.sh
  (optional, on AVX-512: SIMD_LEVELS="default:,v4:-march=x86-64-v4" SIMD_CC=clang mix run bench/simd/time.exs 9)
Record lscpu, the clang version and the load, then fill the 'Not measured: x86-64 timings' table in simd.md.
Deferred with the epic. What remains is only the x86-64 timing run on real hardware (commands in the comment above); the research doc and its recommendation are on main.

title: Research: vectorisation headroom and what target levels buy
